exchanges: Morning. Up early because the bin lorry woke me.
Bin lorries have no mercy. Did you manage to drift off again?
Nope. Made coffee instead. Elena's on nights this week so she just got home.
Night shifts are tough. Does she work at the hospital?
Yeah, maternity. She's a midwife, delivered three babies last night apparently.
That's an incredible night's work. She must be exhausted.
She went straight to bed. We have to be quiet till 2.
Good of everyone to keep it down for her.
Hamza's already out. He goes to the park every Saturday to play chess with the old men by the fountain.
That sounds like a lovely tradition. Is he any good?
He says he wins half the time. They take it very seriously.
Half the time against seasoned park players is pretty respectable.
I think so. Saw Mr Dubois walking his dog on the way back from the shop.
Is he the neighbour on the corner?
Yeah, number 14. His dog is a beagle called Margot, she's so friendly.
Margot sounds sweet. Dogs like that tend to love everyone.
She does. Rent's due Monday, need to remind everyone.
A group message might save chasing people.
Good idea. Our landlady's quite strict about dates.
Better to be early then.
Funny thing, she's called Elena too. So we have house Elena and landlady Elena.
That must make texts confusing. Do you nickname them?
Landlady Elena is 'Mrs P'. She's an accountant, so she notices if we're even a pound short.
Makes sense that she's precise with numbers. Exact amounts it is.
Exactly. The Polish deli has a new sourdough by the way.
Ooh, worth trying. Is it good?
Very. Got two loaves.
One for now and one for the freezer, smart.
The kid next door was out playing badminton against the wall again.
Persistent practice. Does he ever hit the windows?
Once. Mr Dubois was not amused.
Ha, I can imagine.
Actually, I was wrong about Margot. Mr Dubois told me today she's a basset, not a beagle. Long ears, short legs. I should have known.
Ha, the ears are the giveaway. Easy to mix up at a glance though.
She does look a bit like a stretched beagle.
That's a fair description, honestly.
Elena's awake now. Earlier than expected.
Maybe the bin lorry got her too.
Probably. She wants to try the new Korean place for lunch.
Nice, a new spot is always worth a look.
We just got back. She had the bibimbap and said it was the best she's had outside Seoul.
High praise. Sounds like a new regular spot.
I had dumplings. Also great.
Good to hear both dishes hit the mark.
We'll go back next week for sure.
Sounds like a plan.

questions.message: What's my housemate Elena's job again?
What does Hamza get up to on Saturdays?
Mr Dubois has a beagle, doesn't he?
What did Elena order at the Korean place?
What does Hamza do for work?
I might take a nap this afternoon, I'm so full.
